readings.title: The path missing from the map
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Meadow Mapping Project asked residents to mark routes they used regularly. A narrow path behind the shops appeared in many replies but not on the printed town map. Before adding it, volunteers checked whether it was public and whether access changed at night. They discovered that part crossed private land with permission limited to daylight hours. The community map included the route with that condition clearly stated. Local knowledge had identified a useful connection, but checking its status prevented misleading advice. A map could serve newcomers only if its attractive shortcuts were described accurately.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: A crossing seen at walking speed
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A planning team assessed a neighbourhood crossing from photographs and found it clear. Residents who used walking aids reported a different experience: the green signal ended before they comfortably reached the other side. Volunteers timed the crossing with permission and recorded the route to the button as well as the road width. The report gave planners specific observations to investigate. It did not require claiming that every pedestrian moved at the same pace. Looking at the crossing through actual journeys revealed a problem that a still image could not show.

readings.title: The useful place and the private home
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Volunteers making a neighbourhood map wanted to identify residents who could help newcomers. One suggested marking the homes of people with practical skills. Others pointed out that willingness to help at a community event did not mean permission to publish a home address. The group instead listed a shared contact point where residents could offer help voluntarily. The map remained useful without exposing personal locations. More information was not always better information. The organisers learnt to ask whether a detail was necessary for the map's purpose and whether the person concerned had agreed to share it.

readings.title: A map with a date
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community map marked a drinking fountain that had been removed during building work. After a visitor reported the error, volunteers realised they had no regular update process. They added a publication date, a way to report changes and a schedule for checking frequently used facilities. They also distinguished temporary closures from permanent removal. The map would never remain accurate without attention, but users could now judge its age and contribute corrections. Maintaining information was less visible than launching the original project. It was equally important to the trust that made the map useful.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

A map reflects decisions about what is important enough to show. Residents may notice a useful path or a difficult crossing that a general map leaves out. Their knowledge can improve local information, provided it is checked and updated. A useful map also respects the privacy of the people who live there.
translation.referenceAnswer: 地图体现了对哪些信息重要到值得标示的判断。居民可能注意到一般地图遗漏的实用小路或难以通过的路口。只要这些信息经过核实和更新，他们的知识就能改善本地信息。实用的地图还应尊重当地居民的隐私。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

criteria.name: 意义完整与准确
criteria.description: 准确传达各句核心信息、对象和逻辑关系；按遗漏或误译程度酌情扣分。

criteria.name: 中文表达
criteria.description: 中文自然通顺，句间衔接合理；不拘泥于英语词序。

criteria.name: 细节与规范
criteria.description: 关键词译法贴合语境，指代清楚，标点和文字规范。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Write a plan for a community map useful to newcomers. Explain what information to include, how to check it, and how to protect personal privacy.
writing.sampleAnswer: A community map for newcomers should show useful public places, walking connections and access information, such as steps or limited opening hours. Residents could suggest details, but volunteers should check them with site managers or direct observation before publication. Each edition should carry a date and offer a simple way to report changes. Frequently used routes and facilities should be checked regularly. The map should avoid publishing private home addresses or personal details without clear permission. If residents wish to offer help, a shared contact point would be safer and easier to maintain. A useful map is not the one containing the most information. It is the one whose relevant information people can understand, trust and keep current.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
